sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the 5th respondent, Insurance Company in O.P (MV) No.686 of 2004 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thodupuzha.
The respondents herein were the petitioners and the respondents 1 to 4 before the tribunal.

2. The facts leading to the case before the tribunal is as follows:- On 09.02.2004, while the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-7U/8423, a bus bearing Reg.No.6/8647 stopped ahead of the motorcycle abruptly and the motorcycle hit on the left back side of the bus and thereby he sustained serious injuries resulting in his death.
The legal heirs approached the tribunal claiming compensation under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
3. Before the tribunal, the 1st respondent is the driver of the bus.
The 2nd and 4th respondents are the registered owners of the bus and the motorcycle respectively.
The 3rd and 5th respondents are the insurers of the bus and the motorcycle ridden by the deceased respectively.

The respondent Nos.

before the tribunal

. The 3 rd respondent filed a 2025:KER:50786 MACA NO. 1827 OF 2008 written statement admitting the insurance policy for the bus and contended that the accident occurred due to the rashness and negligence of the deceased.
The 5 th respondents admitted the policy of the motorcycle and contended that the negligence was on the part of the driver of the bus.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A6 series and Exts.B1, B2 were marked.
PWs1 and 2 were examined.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, found that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the bus and the 3rd and 5th respondents being the insurers were found liable to pay the compensation.
The tribunal awarded a total compensation of 2,76,500/- with interest @ 8% per annum.

Challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the 5th respondent,
insurance company have come up with this appeal.

4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant insurer, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 8th respondent.
5.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant insurer submits that the legal heirs of the deceased 2025:KER:50786 MACA NO. 1827 OF 2008 have filed the original petition seeking compensation from the insurer of the offending vehicle, which is a bus bearing Reg.No.KL-6/8647.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant insurer submits that the claim was filed under Section 163A of the Act and there was no necessity to prove or plead any negligence on the part of the rider as well as the driver of the offending vehicle.
The standing counsel further submits that the policy issued by the insurer of the motorcycle was only an Act-only policy.

Since the deceased was the rider of the motorcycle and the claim petition was filed arraying the owner and the insurer of the motorcycle as well as owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, the tribunal has found that the driver of the bus as well as the rider of the motorcycle were negligent, causing the accident.
The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 8th respondent insurer of the bus submits that the tribunal has found joint and several liability on the rider as well as the driver of the bus.
Thus, the tribunal directed both the insurance companies to pay the compensation amount equally.
However, the appellant insurer challenges the finding of 50% contributory negligence fixed on the part of the rider, in a claim petition filed under Section 163A of the Act.
I have considered the rival contentions raised by both sides.
7. First of all, this is a petition filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, wherein the negligence of the rider as well as the driver has no relevance.

Since the legal heirs of the deceased have put a claim against the offending vehicle, the tribunal ought not to have found that there was negligence on the part of both the rider and the driver of the vehicles and directed both insurance companies to pay the amount equally.
Since the policy issued to the motorcycle was an act only policy, the insurer of the motorcycle cannot be held liable to pay any compensation since the deceased was the rider of the motorcycle.
He will step into the shoes of the owner and hence is not entitled to claim compensation from the insurer of the motorcycle.

However, the claim against the insurer of the offending vehicle is legally sustainable since it is a petition filed under Section 163A of National Insurance Co.Ltd vs Purushothaman on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157968850/
3 the Act.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I find that the direction of the tribunal, finding negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and directing the appellant insurer to pay 50% of the award amount is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The direction of the 2025:KER:50786 MACA NO. 1827 OF 2008 tribunal directing the appellant insurer herein to pay 50% of the compensation amount awarded by the tribunal is hereby set aside.
It is made clear that the 8th respondent in the appeal, the Oriental Insurance Company Limited is liable to pay the entire compensation awarded by the tribunal with interest and costs.
